newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Feb 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Feb 26.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Wednesday:

* In a memo to his staff two years ago, President Clinton endorsed a plan to reward top contributors to the Democratic Party with invitations to the White House for overnight stays in the Lincoln bedroom, golf outings and morning jogs.

* A private secretary for a top official in Mexico's governing party has disclosed to American authorities a series of dealings between drug traffickers and high-ranking politicians, including family members of former President Carlos Salinas de Gortari.

* A deal between Rupert Murdoch's News Corp and EchoStar to create a new satellite service that could be the first full-fledged competitor to cable television has shaken the industry. The service, in which Murdoch is investing $1 billion, would be able to beam 500 channels of programming.
* Contributors and fund raisers said invitations to White House coffees were explicitly sold in exchange for donations ranging from $50,000 to as much as $100,000.
* Mexico said any move by the United States to downgrade Mexico's standing as an anti-drug ally would damage relations between the countries and Mexico's drug-fighting efforts.

* The gunman who killed one tourist and wounded seven others at the Empire State Building before fatally shooting himself left behind a note saying he wanted to avenge the way the U.S., Israel and other countries treated Palestinians.

* Chinese President Jiang Zemin promised to continue the policies of Deng Xiaoping in a eulogy delivered before 10,000 people attending Deng's funeral inside the Great Hall of the People at Tiananmen Square.

* Florida authorities charged an Orthodox Jew named Harry Shapiro with planting a bomb at a Conservative Jewish synangogue where former Israeli Prime Minister Shimon Peres spoke on February 13. The bomb, which did not explode, was found nine days later by children attending a luncheon after a bar mitzvah.
